code.originalText: Primary care visit three weeks after completing chemoradiation directed by the head and neck oncology team

text.paragraph: Primary care review three weeks after chemoradiation. [S]

Mr. Grant returns three weeks after finishing chemoradiation, directed by the head and neck oncology team, for p16-negative squamous cell carcinoma of the right tonsillar pillar. His throat pain has eased to 3 of 10. He takes the acetaminophen solution once or twice a day and rarely needs the lidocaine rinse. His mouth is dry and food tastes muted, so he sips water with every mouthful. He eats soft foods with two supplement drinks a day and did not need a feeding tube. He weighs 71.0 kg, 7 kg below his weight at intake. He has smoked no cigars since mid-July and continues varenicline 1 mg twice daily without side effects. His energy is slowly returning and he writes for two to three hours a day. He has had no fever, bleeding, choking, or new lumps in the neck, and no change in his hearing. He uses fluoride gel in trays each night, as the dentist advised before radiation. [S]
